summary.intent: Enable test calls for the voice assistant without real telephony by routing them through a teammate's (Akshat's) dashboard branch, with a possible later PWA that sends a notification and starts a call on tap.
summary.outcome: Created a branch based on akshat/dashboard and added a voice call feature: a new backend module (voice.py), a React VoiceCall component, and hooks into his API route and detail view. The build was typechecked and the voice session route was test-started, but the transcript doesn't show the results. The PWA stage has not been started.

repo: Akshat's branch akshat/dashboard is a 'decision inbox' built with FastAPI and React: modules drop cards (JSON) with options and draft messages, and people decide in the browser (allow once / allow always / edit / dismiss).
Decisions are persisted to data/state/decisions.json, which is the shared contract. Voice and Twilio call outcomes should both write through it so everything lands in one inbox.
The dashboard has an 'ask' vs 'autonomous' mode and already uses the team's watcher store for its activity feed (changes, mails).
Team workflow: don't change a teammate's work unannounced; build on your own branch based on theirs with minimal edits to their files (here: one new module, one route, one component).
Mapping for voice decisions: approve -> allow_once, reject -> dismiss, escalate -> note for next person.

Architecture: POST /api/cards/{id}/voice returns a short-lived OpenAI key with the card content as instructions; the browser talks to GPT-Realtime over WebRTC (no Twilio); Twilio phone calls stay for critical cards.

code.finding: Card detail view in Akshat's dashboard; the VoiceCall component was hooked in right above the decision buttons.
New module that creates the short-lived OpenAI Realtime session for a card, exposed via a new route in Akshat's API.

workflow: Telegram bot API can't place calls; real Telegram calls need a user account with unofficial libs like pytgcalls (ban risk, 2-3h). WhatsApp business calling needs a verified Meta business account (days). Browser WebRTC is the cheapest test path.
Planned staging: first browser voice button, then a PWA with push notification whose tap opens the app and auto-starts the voice conversation.

friction: Real-call alternatives (Telegram, WhatsApp, Teams, Discord) are each impractical for quick testing due to API limits, account-ban risk, or approval delays.
The feature requires touching a teammate's files, so coordination with Akshat is needed before merge.
open_items: Build the PWA: installable dashboard, push notification for critical cards, tap to auto-start the voice conversation.
Notify Akshat and get his merge of the jonas/voice-dashboard branch.
Verify the result of the typecheck/build and the voice session route test, which are not shown in the transcript.
Wire voice outcomes (approve/reject/escalate) to the decisions endpoint and confirm Twilio critical-card calls also write to decisions.json.
